Oil and Oilseeds Sectional Committee, PAD 44

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau cf Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Orlseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. India is importing a huge quantity of rapeseed oil and rapeseeds for the past many years. The western countries have carried out extensive work to alter the rapeseed genetically. The objective of this change is two-fold - to reduce the erucic acid content and to reduce the glucosinolate content in the rapeseed. This has resulted in producing varieties of rapeseed which have almost zero percent erucic acid and very low glucosinolate content. Indian rapeseeds contain about 45 percent erucic acid. The reduction in erucic acid is accompanied by an increase in the oleic acid. Therefore, the iodine value of the low erucic acid rapeseed oil is higher than the normal Indian rapeseed oil. Also, because of the reduction in high molecular weight erucic acid, the saponification value of such an oil is higher than the normal Indian rapeseed oil. However all the rapeseeds produced in the western countries are not of low erucic varieties. The erucic acid content may vary from 0 to SO percent in the rapeseed grown abroad.

Low erucic rapeseed oil, with less than 5 percent erucic acid, contains 45�65 percent oleic acid, 15-25 percent linoleic acid and 7-13 percent linolenic acid as the major fatty acids. High erucic rapeseed oil, with erucic acid more than 40 percent contains 12-20 percent oleic acid, 15-25 percent linoleic acid, 7-13 percent linolenic acid and 40�~O percent erucic acid as the major fatty acids. The varieties having erucic acid between 5 and 50 percent will show proportional increase in tbe oleic acid content as the erucic acid content is reduced.
This Indian Standard has been formulated to prescribe the requirements for the two varieties of imported rapeseed oil being used in the country: (a) those containing up to S percent erucic acid, and (b) those containing above S percent erucic acid. The requirements of this standard take care of the prov isions of the Prevention ation Act, 1954 and Rules framed thereunder. .

0/ Food Adulter-

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed 'cr calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded eft' value should be the same as tbat of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard
IMPORTED RAPESEED OIL - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for imported rapeseed oil. 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 11476 : 1985 and those given below shalt apply. 3.1 Imported Rapeseed Oil - Imported rapeseed oil means: a) The oil obtained from clean and sound rapeseed grown abroad or rapeseed cake belonging to campestris or napus varieties of Brassica, by the method of expression or solvent extraction and imported into India, or b) The oil produced in India from clean and sound imported rapeseed or rapeseed cake belonging to campestrls or napus varieties of Brassica, by the method of expression or solvent extraction. 3.2 Refined Imported Rapeseed Oil Imported rapeseed oil obtained by the process

4.1 Varieties
The material shall be of two varieties, one containing erucic acid 5 percent maximum and the other containing erucic acid above 5 percent. The variety shall be decided by finding the fatty acid composition of the oil using gas liquid chromatographic method prescribed in IS 548 ( Part 3 ) : 1976.
